result.title: 3D Diffusion Models for Medical Imaging
result.comment: 27 pages, accepted for publication in Informatics in Medicine Unlocked
result.summary: Generative deep learning methods such as Variational Autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks or Diffusion Models have achieved remarkable results in image synthesis. In particular, Diffusion Models have demonstrated superior image fidelity and sample diversity compared to other approaches on standard benchmarks, while also offering more flexible training dynamics as evidenced both in natural image domains and in medical applications. In medical imaging including Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Positron Emission Tomography, such models have various important use-cases including data augmentation, domain transfer, image reconstruction, inpainting, image augmentation and artifact correction. Further, generated images can be conditioned on patient characteristics, medical reports, segmentation masks or other images. Specific challenges arise due to the 3D volumetric nature of medical images, which translate to substantial demands in terms of memory, compute, and training data. This article provides a comparative overview of 3D Diffusion Models which have been developed for medical images, with a focus on current performance, limitations, and an outlook for future work.
